f1.quote: substituted Co for Ni by increasing x from 0.40 to 0.55

f2.quote: annealed at 750 °C for 72 h in high vacuum, and water-quenched

f3.quote: DSC was performed from 183–400 K at 10 K min−1 under N2

f4.quote: isothermal magnetization/entropy measurements used fields up to 5 T near TC

f5.quote: stabilized the high-temperature hexagonal Ni2In-type phase, shifted the hexagonal-to-orthorhombic TiNiSi-type transformation downward

f6.quote: changed the transition from coupled first-order magnetostructural behavior for x = 0.40–0.50 to a second-order magnetic transition for x = 0.55

f7.quote: When the structural transition lies near TC, coupling between ferromagnetic TiNiSi-type martensite and paramagnetic Ni2In-type austenite produces latent heat, hysteresis, and a giant magnetocaloric response; loss of this coupling at x = 0.55 yields a small second-order response.

f8.quote: increasing Co substitution was found to progressively lower Ttr, TC, and peak magnetic entropy change, eventually suppressing the giant first-order magnetocaloric effect at x = 0.55

f9.quote: with its structural transition outside the DSC range of 183–400 K

f10.quote: increasing Co substitution was found to progressively lower Ttr, TC, and peak magnetic entropy change

f11.quote: Direct ΔTad was measured with 120 s in-field residence, 180 mm s−1 sample motion, and 0.5 K min−1 heating under a 5 T superconducting field and a 4.8 T pulsed field.

f12.quote: generally increasing hardness and giving the highest compressive strength at x = 0.55
